pages.name: Which way will it tip?
pages.task: A 4 N weight hangs 30 cm left of the pivot and a 6 N weight 15 cm right. Which way will the bar tip?
pages.why: The 4 N turns the bar with 4 × 30 = 120 N cm. The 6 N turns it the other way with 6 × 15 = 90 N cm. The bigger turning effect wins. So the left side goes down, even though its weight is lighter.

pages.name: Where it balances
pages.task: A 3 N weight hangs 20 cm right of the pivot. How far left of the pivot must a 5 N weight hang to balance it?
pages.why: 3 × 20 = 60 N cm clockwise. The 5 N must make 60 N cm too. So it hangs 60 ÷ 5 = 12 cm out.

pages.name: Read the rule
pages.task: A metre rule is pivoted at its 50 cm mark. A 3 N weight hangs at its 10 cm mark. At which mark must a 4 N weight hang to balance it?
pages.why: The 3 N hangs 50 − 10 = 40 cm from the pivot. So it makes 3 × 40 = 120 N cm. The 4 N must make 120 N cm too. So it hangs 120 ÷ 4 = 30 cm out, at the 50 + 30 = 80 cm mark. The rule is pivoted at its middle. So its own weight turns nothing.

pages.name: Add each side
pages.text: With two weights on one side, add their moments. Clockwise, 3 × 10 + 1.5 × 20 = 60 N cm. Anticlockwise, 2 × 30 = 60 N cm. The totals match, so the bar hangs level. Yet the right carries 4.5 N and the left only 2 N.

pages.name: Three weights
pages.task: A 5 N weight hangs 24 cm left of the pivot. On the right, a 4 N weight hangs 15 cm out. How far out on the right must a 3 N weight hang to level the bar?
pages.why: Anticlockwise, 5 × 24 = 120 N cm. Clockwise, the 4 N makes 4 × 15 = 60 N cm. The 3 N must make up the other 60 N cm. So it hangs 60 ÷ 3 = 20 cm out.

pages.name: Fold a level
pages.text: The lower bar balances, because 2 × 10 = 20 N cm and 4 × 5 = 20 N cm. Folded, it becomes one 6 N weight on the hook. The hook is 20 cm left of the top pivot. So the top bar feels 6 × 20 = 120 N cm from it, folded or not.

pages.name: The mystery weight
pages.task: A lower bar hangs 20 cm left of the top pivot. On it, 2 N hangs 10 cm left of its string and 4 N hangs 5 cm right. A box hangs 30 cm right of the top pivot. How much must the box weigh to level the top bar?
pages.why: The lower level weighs 2 + 4 = 6 N at its hook. So it makes 6 × 20 = 120 N cm anticlockwise. The box must make 120 N cm clockwise. So it weighs 120 ÷ 30 = 4 N.

pages.name: The crane arm
pages.task: A crane arm is 14 m long. It weighs 12 kN, acting at its middle. It pivots 4 m from its back end. A 20 kN load hangs from its front end, 10 m from the pivot. What counterweight at the back end holds the arm level?
pages.why: The arm's middle is 7 m from its back end. That puts it 3 m in front of the pivot. Clockwise, 20 × 10 + 12 × 3 = 200 + 36 = 236 kN m. The counterweight hangs 4 m out. So it must weigh 236 ÷ 4 = 59 kN. These are example figures, not a real crane's.

pages.name: Two unknowns
pages.task: A lower bar hangs 15 cm left of the top pivot. A hangs 10 cm left of its string and B 20 cm right. A 6 N weight hangs 15 cm right of the top pivot. The whole mobile hangs level. What does A weigh?
pages.why: Both distances on the top bar are 15 cm. So A + B = 6 N. On the lower bar, A × 10 = B × 20. So A is twice B. Twice B plus B is 6 N. So B = 2 N and A = 4 N.

pages.name: The see-saw
pages.task: A 250 N child sits 2.4 m from a see-saw's pivot. How far from the pivot must a 750 N adult sit to balance?
pages.why: 250 × 2.4 = 600 N m. The adult must make 600 N m too. So the adult sits 600 ÷ 750 = 0.8 m out.

pages.name: Which way now?
pages.task: A 5 N weight hangs 12 cm left of the pivot. On the right, 3 N hangs 18 cm out and 1 N hangs 6 cm out. Which way will the bar go?
pages.why: Anticlockwise, 5 × 12 = 60 N cm. Clockwise, 3 × 18 + 1 × 6 = 54 + 6 = 60 N cm. The totals match, so the bar stays level.
